params.question: According to Winslow's definition, which of the following best describes the distinguishing feature of public health compared to clinical medicine?

answers.text: It relies primarily on curative interventions delivered in hospital settings

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Curative hospital-based care is characteristic of clinical medicine. Public health, by contrast, emphasises prevention through organised community efforts at the population level.

answers.text: It focuses on preventing disease and promoting health through organised community efforts at the population level

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Winslow (1920) described public health as the science and art of preventing disease through organised community action, with the population — not the individual patient — as the unit of concern.

answers.text: It uses advanced diagnostic techniques to prolong individual patient survival

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Advanced diagnostics and individual patient care fall under clinical medicine. Public health uses epidemiology, biostatistics, and health communication to protect populations.

answers.text: It addresses only communicable diseases through quarantine and isolation measures

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Public health has a much broader scope — including non-communicable diseases, nutrition, environmental sanitation, mental health, and health-systems strengthening.

overallFeedback.feedback: Winslow defined public health as the science and art of preventing disease through organised community efforts. Its focus is the population, not the individual patient, and it complements — not competes with — clinical medicine.
Winslow emphasised that public health works through organised community structures to prevent disease and promote health — its unit of concern is the population, not the individual patient.

interactions.label: Which landmark report first proposed a comprehensive framework of health determi

params.question: Which landmark report first proposed a comprehensive framework of health determinants — human biology, environment, lifestyle, and health-care organisation — shifting the focus away from a purely biomedical model?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Bhore Committee (1946) recommended restructuring India's health services but did not propose a comprehensive health-determinants framework of the kind described here.
The Alma-Ata Declaration (1978) championed primary health care and 'Health for All' but did not originate the four-category determinants framework. It came four years after Lalonde.

Correct. The Lalonde Report (Canada, 1974) identified four broad categories of health determinants — human biology, environment, lifestyle, and health-care organisation — marking a paradigm shift away from the purely biomedical model.

answers.text: The WHO Commission on Social Determinants of Health, 2008

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Marmot Commission (2008) powerfully reinforced the importance of social determinants but built upon the Lalonde framework, which came over three decades earlier.

overallFeedback.feedback: The Lalonde Report (Canada, 1974) first proposed this comprehensive four-category framework. The WHO Commission (Marmot, 2008) later reinforced the social-determinants perspective, but the conceptual shift began with Lalonde.

The Lalonde Report (Canada, 1974) was the landmark document that identified four broad determinant categories and shifted thinking beyond biology alone. Park's textbook further adapts this into five categories for the Indian context.

interactions.label: In the natural history of disease, the 'iceberg phenomenon' (Gordon, 1952) refer

params.question: In the natural history of disease, the 'iceberg phenomenon' (Gordon, 1952) refers to:

answers.text: The tendency of epidemics to spread most rapidly in the earliest days before containment measures take effect

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: That describes epidemic dynamics, not the iceberg phenomenon. The iceberg metaphor specifically refers to the ratio of hidden sub-clinical cases to visible clinical ones.

answers.text: The large proportion of sub-clinical, undiagnosed cases that remain hidden beneath a smaller number of clinically apparent cases

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. For diseases like TB, dengue, and poliomyelitis, the diagnosed clinical cases are merely the visible tip, while a much larger mass of sub-clinical infection goes undetected — this hidden burden has major implications for disease transmission and control.

answers.text: The irreversible progression from the period of pathogenesis to death without any possibility of recovery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The natural history of disease can end in recovery, disability, or death — it is not always irreversible. The iceberg phenomenon refers to hidden sub-clinical cases, not disease outcomes.

answers.text: The delay between initial agent exposure and the appearance of the first clinical symptoms

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: That delay is called the incubation period. The iceberg phenomenon specifically describes the large hidden burden of sub-clinical cases relative to the smaller number of diagnosed ones.

overallFeedback.feedback: The iceberg phenomenon (Gordon, 1952) describes how the clinically apparent cases of a disease are only the small visible tip, while a much larger mass of sub-clinical, undiagnosed cases lies hidden — driving transmission and complicating control efforts.

The iceberg phenomenon highlights that for many diseases, the diagnosed cases are only the visible tip. The much larger sub-clinical mass below drives ongoing transmission and makes population-level screening essential.

interactions.label: Life expectancy at birth is classified as a mortality indicator because it is ca

params.question: Life expectancy at birth is classified as a mortality indicator because it is calculated from death rates.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Life expectancy is indeed calculated from mortality data, but it is classified as a positive health indicator, not a mortality indicator. Positive health indicators capture actual good health and functional capacity — not just the absence of death. Mortality indicators include crude death rate and infant mortality rate.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Although life expectancy is derived from mortality data, it is classified as a positive health indicator because it captures overall health achievement and functional capacity of a population, not merely the pattern of death.

interactions.label: India's infant mortality rate dropped from 80 to 32 per 1,000 live births nation

params.question: India's infant mortality rate dropped from 80 to 32 per 1,000 live births nationally, yet maternal mortality ranges from 19 per 100,000 in Kerala to over 200 in Assam. Which conclusion about health planning is best supported by this data?

answers.text: Declining infant mortality proves that all states have achieved uniformly good population health

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: National averages mask enormous interstate variation. A state like Assam has maternal mortality more than ten times that of Kerala — a single national figure hides these disparities entirely.

answers.text: National averages can mask critical interstate variation, so effective health planning requires disaggregated, region-specific indicators

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. India's wide interstate variation means a single national figure is misleading. States in earlier demographic transition need maternal-child health services and family planning, while states further along need chronic disease prevention — one formula cannot serve both.

answers.text: Maternal mortality is inherently more reliable than infant mortality and should replace it as the sole planning metric

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: No single indicator can capture a population's health on its own. Maternal mortality and infant mortality measure different dimensions — both are needed together with other indicators to guide planning.

answers.text: Since the total fertility rate has reached replacement level nationally, family planning programmes are no longer needed in any state

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The national TFR is 2.0, but states like Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Meghalaya remain above replacement level. Uniform withdrawal of family planning would ignore these ongoing needs.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key lesson is that national averages can be misleading. India's demographic and health indicators vary widely between states, so health planning must be region-specific — MCH services where transition is early, NCD prevention where it is advanced.

India's demographic data shows that national averages mask enormous interstate variation. Effective health planning must use disaggregated indicators and tailor interventions to each region's stage in the demographic transition.
